text: Art.1. In every occupation the oldest and the most experienced are to take turns, according to seniority, and for five days at a time, in directing five or six of their companions, and are to fix the scale of work to be performed by them, moderately, on the basis of the amount which has been imposed upon themselves.
Art. 2. In every occupation there is to be one master for ten or twenty workmen.
Art. 7. The heads of every occupation are to appoint the hours of rest and of labour, and to prescribe what is to be done.
